text: {"cases":[{"id":"C01","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C01-R2","C01-A"]],"reason":"C01-R2 reports the 2023 anomaly as 2.1 °C, explicitly stating the unit is Celsius, for the same analysis, metric, and 1951–1980 baseline. C01-A reports about 1.2 °C for that baseline and lists 2.1 only as the Fahrenheit value. The two statements cannot both be true in Celsius, so the summary misstated the unit."},{"id":"C02","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C02-R3","C02-A"]],"reason":"For Orion 4.2 under the default configuration with no exception, C02-A says unsigned extensions may not execute and C02-R3 says they may. These are direct contradictions, regardless of C02-R3 being a derived summary."},{"id":"C03","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C03-R6","C03-A"]],"reason":"Both describe the final settled total refund for INV-204 on 2025-02-18 in USD, including all adjustments, but give USD 183.00 and USD 138.00."},{"id":"C04","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C04-R6","C04-A"]],"reason":"Both concern the final audit of the same 37 units in batch B17. NASA gives about 1.2 °C above its 1951–1980 baseline, and NOAA gives 1.18 °C above a different, 20th-century, baseline. They differ in baseline and source analysis, not necessarily in fact."},{"id":"C08","status":"compatible","pairs":[],"reason":"The periods are different: C08-A covers March 2025 and C08-R3 covers April 2025.
